land.text: the Oirat lands of western Mongolia (Hovd, Uvs, Bayan-Olgii, Dzavhan, Tuva and the Mongolian Altai)

predecessors.note: The infobox says 'Preceded by: Northern Yuan'; 'Möngke-Temür, a high official of the Yuan, had placed himself at the head of the Oirats' in 1399. Cliopatria carves the shape (3,352 cells) out of its Northern Yuan row in 1402.

land.text: the Dzungarian core (Cliopatria's Oirat Confederation shape of 1619, the same cells as its Dzungar row of 1609), where the Oirats 'united in the Junggar Basin in Dzungaria' about 1620

successors.note: The same Oirat people: the Oirat Confederation page (infobox '1399-1634') treats one confederation, and the oirat-confederation dossier (found 1609, counterpart this slug) is the later Cliopatria row (Wikidata Q4332415 is shared). This dossier now runs on to 1608 (fx-51, life-span gap).

land.text: the rest of the old Oirat west that the Dzungarian core does not take: western Mongolia, which the Mongol Khanate's Cliopatria row (1468-1635) covers

successors.note: Modelling note, not a page date: the pages give no year in which the Oirats left western Mongolia (they 'looted' by the Khalkhas 'in the Irtysh, Barkol and Altai from 1552 to 1628'); without this entry the compiler would hand those cells to nobody at the end of 1608.

rulers.name: Mahamu (Mahmud) with Taiping and Batu-bolad
rulers.note: After Möngke-Temür's death 'three chieftains, Mahamu (Mahmud), Taiping and Batu-bolad, ruled them'; the Yongle Emperor gave them the title of wang in 1409; Mahamu of Choros killed Öljei Temür in 1412.

rulers.name: Toghan (Toghon)
rulers.note: Son of Mahamu, succeeded in 1408; died 1438; defeated Arugtai and Adai Khan by 1437.

rulers.name: Esen Taishi
rulers.note: Taishi 1438-1454; declared himself Great Khan of the Northern Yuan in 1453 (Tian-sheng Khagan of the Great Yuan); killed in 1455 (infobox).

rulers.name: Amasanj
rulers.note: Esen's son, given the taishi title; moved west pillaging Hami, Moghulistan and the Uzbeks.

rulers.name: Ishtömör
rulers.note: Listed as ruler 1455-1469 on the Oirat Confederation page; no further list for 1469-1480.

correction.text: the 1402 shape taken back to 1399: the Oirat homeland of western Mongolia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1399-1401: Cliopatria starts in 1402, the page's confederation dates from 1399 ('Möngke-Temür places himself at the head of the Oirats'). The 1402 shape (3,357 cells, 912,000 km2) taken back three years; no infobox area on the page.

912,000 km2: Hovd, Uvs, Bayan-Olgii, Dzavhan, most of Hovsgol and Tuva and the Mongolian Altai, cut out of Cliopatria's Northern Yuan row. The Northern Yuan page has the Oirat-backed Orug Temur beaten by Oljei Temur in 1403 and the Oirats under Mahamu enthroning a khan in 1412; the Oirat page has Mahamu killing Oljei Temur in 1412: a homeland shape for a period of struggle with the eastern khans.
Same extent as 1402 (3,355 cells). The Oirat page has no territorial event 1415-1421; Mahamu's son Toghan succeeded him in 1408 and kept 'his strife with Arugtai chingsang'.

Valid 1422-1433: the 1415 shape plus 739 cells taken from Cliopatria's Chagatai row, i.e. the Oirat grazing lands 'east of Lake Balkash' where Uwais Khan (1418-1428) was 'usually defeated and even captured twice by the Oirat Esen Tayishi'. From 1434 the new keyframe takes over.

correction.text: the 1440 shape for 1434-1439: all Mongolia, Tuva, Buryatia, Chita, a third of Inner Mongolia and Dzungaria

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1434-1439: 'resulting in Arughtai's death in 1434' (Esen page; the Northern Yuan page has Arughtai pushed east of the Khingan range in 1433 and killed the next year); Toghon then installed Taisun as puppet Great Khan, and 'By 1437, Toghan had totally defeated Arugtai and an Ogedeid Emperor Adai Khan' (Oirat page). Esen 'conquered Outer Mongolia and Inner Mongolia' (undated). Cliopatria's 1440 shape (14,127 cells, 3.42 M km2) takes in all Mongolia, Buryatia, Chita and a third of Inner Mongolia; it is the shape for these years.
Valid 1440-1446. The Esen page has Hami attacked in 1443 and 1445 and the Uriankhai guards conquered by 1447; Cliopatria adds the Manchurian and Inner Mongolian lands only in 1450.

correction.text: the 1450 shape for 1447-1449: Mongolia plus Inner Mongolia and the Daning and Duoyan guard lands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1447-1449: 'By 1447, Esen had conquered the Daning and Duoyan guards' and forced the Fuyu to migrate (the Uriankhai Three Guards in Manchuria and Inner Mongolia); Cliopatria's 1450 shape adds 2,439 cells from the Ming row (Inner Mongolia 0.34 to 0.72).

Valid 1450-1454: 3.96 M km2 (16,566 cells). The Esen page puts the domain 'from present-day Xinjiang (Hami and Turfan area) to Gansu, the Uriankhai lands, and the Korean border'. The Ming war of 1449 (Tumu) and the 1450 peace moved no frontier.

correction.text: the 1468 shape for 1455-1462: the Oirat west, without Mongolia, Inner Mongolia and Manchuria

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1455-1462: 'a series of revolts resulted in Esen's death. His death started the decline of the Oirats'; the Oirat page: 'Esen's death broke up the unity of the Oirats' and Genghisid khans were enthroned by Kharchin, Belguteid and Ordos warlords until 1481. Cliopatria keeps the whole Esen empire until 1467; the 1468 shape (western Mongolia and Dzungaria) is the right extent after the break-up.

correction.text: use the 1468 shape (western Mongolia and Dzungaria) for 1463-1467

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws the full Esen empire (3.96 M km2) for 1463-1467 and hands it to the Mongol Khanate only in 1468, but Esen died in 1455 and the Oirat realm broke up; use the 1468 shape.

1.13 M km2 (4,097 cells), 4,075 in 1422: the Oirat west. Ishtomor is listed as ruler 1455-1469; the Eastern Mongols push the Oirats west from 1480. Moghulistan page: Kyrgyz of the Oirat confederacy move into the Tian Shan in 1469-70 (not drawn).

New keyframe 1475-1480: Cliopatria hands the shape to its Mongol Khanate row in 1475 (3,968 of 4,097 cells), but the Oirat page has the Eastern Mongols push the Oirats westward 'from 1480 on'. [fx-51: the Oirats do not end in 1480; the outline is cut to the Oirat west from 1481 (keyframes _1481 and _1510) and the state runs to 1608.]

correction.text: The Oirat west that remained when 'the Eastern Mongols under Mandukhai Khatun and Dayan Khan pushed the Oirats westward': the 1468 shape cut to western Mongolia, Dzungaria and the Altai (the page has the Oirats' 'properties in the Irtysh, Barkol and Altai' still looted from 1552 to 1628)

keyframe_review.note: Gap years 1481-1509 (fx-51, life-span gap): Cliopatria has no row for the Oirats from 1475 to 1618 and gives the 1474 shape to its Mongol Khanate row; the page keeps the Oirats a separate confederation (1399-1634) and has the Eastern Mongols push them 'westward' from 1480. The 1468 shape (4,097 cells) is cut to the Western Mongolia, Dzungaria and Altai regions (2,306 cells; the Altai region adds the Russian Altai and the Zaysan-Irtysh corner of East Kazakhstan, fx-51 review); confidence 1 for the edge, the page names no border. The land cut away lies north and north-east of the Oirat west (Khovsgol, Tuva, the Sayan and the Baikal west in Krasnoyarsk, Khakassia, Irkutsk and Buryatia) and in the Zhetysu edge of Almaty region; the 1468 shape holds no central Mongolian land (Karakorum, held 'until the 16th century when Altan Khan recaptured the city', lies outside it).

correction.text: The same Oirat west, held to 1608: 'By 1510 Dayan Khan had unified the various Mongol tribes, including the Oirats', yet the Khalkhas 'repeatedly launched massive attacks on the Oirats' and 'looted their properties in the Irtysh, Barkol and Altai from 1552 to 1628'

keyframe_review.note: Gap years 1510-1608 (fx-51): outline unchanged from _1481 (western Mongolia, Dzungaria and the Altai), split at the page's 1510 so that the Oirats' separate existence is stated after Dayan Khan's unification. The page gives no border change in these years; the Oirat west is held until the oirat-confederation dossier (found 1609) draws the Dzungarian core. Confidence 1 for the extent. Whether the Oirats were Dayan Khan's vassals after 1510 is a relation for data/hierarchy.csv; the page says only 'unified'.

region.text: the Oirat lands of western Mongolia

ledger.note: 1399: Mongke-Temur heads the Oirats. 'Mongke-Temur, a high official of the Yuan, had placed himself at the head of the Oirats' (infobox 'Existence ... 1399'); the Oirats 'began to challenge the Borjigin Emperors of the Northern Yuan in the reign of Elbeg Khan (c. 1394-1399)'. The page does not describe an Oirat killing of Elbeg Khan, and gives no boundary; the homeland is the Oirat pastures of western Mongolia.

region.text: the lands east of Lake Balkhash (Dzungaria)

ledger.note: 1422: the Oirats hold the lands east of Lake Balkhash. Uwais Khan (1418-1428) 'was frequently at war with the Oirats who roamed in the area east of Lake Balkash' and was 'usually defeated and even captured twice by the Oirat Esen Tayishi'. The page gives the reign, not a year; 1422 is Cliopatria's shape year (739 of 746 new cells come from its Chagatai row).

region.text: Outer Mongolia, Buryatia and Chita, a third of Inner Mongolia: the Northern Yuan lands

ledger.note: 1434: Arughtai dies and the Oirats rule the Mongols. 'resulting in Arughtai's death in 1434'; Toghon installs Taisun as puppet Great Khan; 'By 1437, Toghan had totally defeated Arugtai and an Ogedeid Emperor Adai Khan' (Oirat page). Esen 'conquered Outer Mongolia and Inner Mongolia' (undated). Cliopatria's shape grows by 9,639 cells from its Northern Yuan row in 1440.

1445: Esen forces Hami and Shazhou to accept Mongol titles. 'Oirats attacked Hami' in 1443; 'In 1445, Esen attacked Hami again and forced Shazhou and Qizhin leaders to accept Mongol titles'; the Oirat page: Esen 'crushed the Moghulistan and Hami monarchs and forced them to accept him as their overlord' (undated). Kara Del of Hami has no Cliopatria row.

region.text: the Daning, Duoyan and Fuyu guard lands in Inner Mongolia and Heilongjiang

ledger.note: 1447: Esen conquers the Uriankhai guards. 'By 1447, Esen had conquered the Daning and Duoyan guards' and forced the Fuyu to migrate; in winter 1450 he and Taisun raided the Jurchens into Heilongjiang. Cliopatria's shape grows by 2,439 cells from the Ming row, Inner Mongolia and Heilongjiang.

1453: Esen proclaims himself Great Khan. 'Esen declared himself the Great Khan of the Northern Yuan' with the title Tian-sheng Khagan of the Great Yuan after murdering Agbarjin; same state, the Oirat taishi becomes khan (rule 2).

1455: Hami is lost with Esen's fall. Page silent on the end of Hami's subordination; bridging judgment from Esen's death in 1455, after which Amasanj 'moved west, pillaging the lands of Hami, Moghulistan and the Uzbegs' (Oirat page).

region.text: Mongolia, Buryatia, Chita, Inner Mongolia and the Manchurian guard lands

ledger.note: 1455: Esen is killed and the empire breaks up. 'a series of revolts resulted in Esen's death. His death started the decline of the Oirats'; Genghisid khans were enthroned by Kharchin, Belguteid and Ordos warlords from Esen's death until 1481. Cliopatria keeps the lands until 1467 and its Mongol Khanate row starts only in 1468, so the Mongol Khanate dossier should start its gain here, not in 1468.

region.text: the northern and north-eastern lands of the 1468 shape outside the Oirat west (Khovsgol, Tuva, the Sayan and the Baikal west in Krasnoyarsk, Khakassia, Irkutsk and Buryatia) and its Zhetysu edge in Almaty region, given up as the Eastern Mongols 'pushed the Oirats westward'

ledger.note: 1480: the Eastern Mongols push the Oirats westward. 'From 1480 on, the Eastern Mongols under Mandukhai Khatun and Dayan Khan pushed the Oirats westward' (Oirat Confederation page, opened as Four Oirat). The page names no land; the part of Cliopatria's 1468 shape outside Western Mongolia, Dzungaria and the Altai is the researcher's reading (confidence 2); the Altai and the Irtysh stay Oirat, where the page has the Khalkhas loot 'their properties in the Irtysh, Barkol and Altai from 1552 to 1628' (fx-51 review). The mongol-khanate dossier has a 1481 gain of the whole shape (ledger 1, confidence 1); see the handoff in the fx-51 report.

region.text: the Oirat west, as held to 1608

ledger.note: 1608: the last year before the oirat-confederation dossier (found 1609, counterpart this slug). The 1480 dissolve into the Mongol Khanate this event replaces was a modelling step, not the end of the Oirats: the page has the Oirats still 'pushed ... westward' from 1480, 'unified' under Dayan Khan by 1510, raided by the Khalkhas 'from 1552 to 1628', and 'united in the Junggar Basin in Dzungaria' about 1620 (Dzungar Khanate); infobox '1399-1634'. The year 1608 is the join with oirat-confederation, not a page date.

wars.name: Oirat-Northern Yuan wars (Toghon against Arughtai and Adai Khan)
wars.outcome: Toghon pushes Arughtai east of the Khingan in 1433, kills him in 1434, installs Taisun as puppet khan and by 1437 has 'totally defeated Arugtai and ... Adai Khan'.
wars.note: The Northern Yuan page: Arughtai 'pushed ... east of the Greater Khingan range in 1433' and killed in the west of Baotou in 1434.

wars.name: Oirat wars with Uwais Khan of Moghulistan

zones.text: the lands east of Lake Balkhash

wars.outcome: Uwais Khan is 'usually defeated and even captured twice' by the Oirats; the Oirats hold the Balkhash-Dzungaria lands.
wars.note: The Esen page gives three campaigns against Eastern Moghulistan in the 1420s.

wars.name: Esen Taishi's campaigns in Hami and against the Uriankhai guards

zones.text: the Daning, Duoyan and Fuyu guards (by 1447)

wars.outcome: Hami is attacked in 1443 and 1445 and Shazhou and Qizhin accept Mongol titles; the Daning and Duoyan guards are conquered by 1447; in winter 1450 Esen and Taisun raid the Jurchens into Heilongjiang.

wars.name: Tumu Crisis
wars.outcome: Esen invades in July 1449, destroys the Ming army at Yanghe (3 August), captures Emperor Yingzong (1 September), besieges Beijing briefly (27-30 August) and returns the emperor in September 1450; no frontier moves.

wars.name: Fall of Esen Taishi

zones.text: the Esen empire east of Dzungaria

wars.outcome: After Esen proclaims himself khan in 1453 Alag rebels and Esen is defeated and killed by Bukun (1455 in the infobox); 'Esen's death broke up the unity of the Oirats'.

wars.name: Mongol recovery of Mongolia from the Oirats
wars.outcome: From 1480 Mandukhai and Dayan Khan push the Oirats west; by 1510 Dayan Khan has unified the Mongol tribes including the Oirats and defeats the southwestern Mongols with the help of the Four Oirats.
wars.note: The Northern Yuan page: Dayan Khan 'finally defeated the southwestern Mongols in 1510' with help from Unebolad wang and the Four Oirats. Reviewer (ia-02-c, 2026-10-19): 'to' trimmed from 1510 to 1480, the dossier's end; the war continues to 1510 after it.

certainty.note: A nomadic confederation without surveyed frontiers: the pages name regions (Hami and Turfan to Gansu, the Uriankhai lands, the Korean border) and peoples, never lines. The Ming frontier near Datong and Beijing in 1449 is the only fixed point. 1481-1608 (fx-51): the outline is the 1468 shape cut to western Mongolia and Dzungaria; the page names no border for the Oirats in these years.

notes:
Two Cliopatria rows share Wikidata Q4332415: 'Four Oirats' (1402-1474, mine) and 'Oirat Confederation' (1619-1676, group ia-03). The Wikipedia page 'Oirat Confederation' treats one confederation from 1399 to 1634 (Dzungar, Kalmyk and Khoshut khanates succeed it) but the two rows are different polities: the 15th-century Oirat realm of the Choros taishis, which dominated the Mongols under Toghon and Esen (1434-1455), and the 17th-century Dzungar-Khoshut-Torghut confederation, with a gap of 143 years (1475-1618) in which the Oirats exist in the Altai and Irtysh without a Cliopatria row. I keep two dossiers; the ia-03 dossier of oirat-confederation should name four-oirats as its predecessor with the Oirat continuity as a note, and decide whether the 1481-1618 Oirat west deserves keyframes of its own.

End year: Cliopatria ends the row in 1474 and gives the whole shape to its Mongol Khanate row in 1475; the Oirat page puts the Eastern Mongol push in 1480 and the Northern Yuan page has the Four Oirats helping Dayan Khan in 1510. I end the dossier in 1480 (new keyframe 1475-1480, dissolve 1480); the Oirats of 1481-1510 in the far west have no shape here.

Capitals: the pages give none (infobox 'Capital(s): Not given'); a nomadic confederation, so the capitals list is empty.

Mongol Khanate: Cliopatria's row starts in 1468, but the Northern Yuan/Oirat pages have Genghisid khans enthroned after Esen's death in 1455 (until 1481); the Mongol Khanate dossier should take the 1455 loss.

Hami: the Oirat suzerainty over Hami (1445-1455) is the only subordination event; Kara Del (Hami, c. 1389-1513 on the disambiguation page) has no Cliopatria row and is a counterpart needing a dossier (group ia-02-x). The Kyrgyz of the Oirat confederacy who moved into the Tian Shan in 1469-70 (Moghulistan page) are not drawn.

Unverified, page budget (5 pages: one a disambiguation page, wasted): the exact 1402 and 1415 outlines of the homeland (Cliopatria's Hovsgol 0.8, Tuva 1.0, Gorno-Altai 0.35); Esen's Manchurian and Korean-border reach beyond the Daning and Duoyan guards; the 1422 date of the Balkhash lands; the 1475 hand-over; Shazhou and Qizhin (Gansu) were forced to accept Mongol titles in 1445 but are not drawn.

Page oddities: 'Mongol_khanate' is a disambiguation page; 'Toghan' (Oirat page) and 'Toghon' (Esen page) are the same man. FX-51 (2 Nov 2026, life-span gap): the dossier no longer ends in 1480. The Oirat Confederation page keeps one confederation (1399-1634) and the oirat-confederation dossier is founded in 1609 with this one as counterpart, so 1481-1608 had no Oirat land. The 1480 dissolve into mongol-khanate became a 1480 loss of the eastern part of the 1468 shape and a dissolve in 1608 into oirat-confederation; keyframes _1481 and _1510 hold the 1468 shape cut to Western Mongolia and Dzungaria (2,112 cells), confidence 1. The mongol-khanate dossier's 1481 gain of the whole shape (ledger 1, confidence 1) must be narrowed to the lost eastern part or the Mongol Khanate takes the Oirat west again (handoff in the fx-51 report).
